page: Microsoft Azure M8ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, the processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AVX-512, and AES instruction sets. The server is equipped with 219.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 27.34 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 262 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the M8ms is optimized primarily for memory-intensive workloads rather than raw compute speed. Single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, fall into the poor to weak categories. However, the server demonstrates average performance in large-block memory write bandwidth and extended CPU instruction tests. LLM inference speeds for small 135M models also reach average tiers, processing 423.6 tokens per second for prompts and 83.59 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized trade-off, offering massive memory density per vCPU at the expense of high-performance compute scaling. It is best suited for workloads requiring large in-memory datasets but moderate CPU processing, such as relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and enterprise applications with high RAM demands.
